textbookText: Inelastic Collision In this collision, only the momentum is conserved but not the KE. i.e, m1u1 +m2u2 = m1v1 +m2v2
There is a loss of KE in the form of sound, heat, or other forms of energy.
The loss of energy, ΔE = {𝟏 m1u12 + 𝟏 m2u22} – {𝟏 m1v12 +𝟏 m2v22}

Since the total mechanical energy in an inelastic collision is converted into other forms of energy such as heat, sound light energy, etc., the forces involved in it are called the nonconservative forces.

Fig 5.16: Inelastic collision, car crash Hence, in an inelastic collision, i) Momentum is conserved ii) KE isn’t conserved iii) Total energy is conserved iv) Mechanical energy is converted into other form of energies. Hence forces involved are non- conservative in nature. For example, when two cars crash and crumple together, a ball of clay is dropped and sticks to the floor, or a tackle in football where players move together after impact. These illustrate how kinetic energy is transformed into other forms of energy during inelastic collisions.
